reflection.quote: The wound is the place where the Light enters you.
reflection.reading:
August in the northern hemisphere has a particular quality — long light, warm evenings, the kind of Saturday that used to be a starting gun. Get up, get moving, meet at the bar by two, see where the night takes us. The math was simple and it was always the same equation.

Sobriety rearranged the whole equation. Now a Saturday in August is a river, or a trail, or a slow coffee on a porch while the day figures itself out. It's making plans I actually keep. It's the strange gift of remembering yesterday. When I was 22 and terrified of what sobriety would take from me, nobody could have described this to me in a way I would have believed. The fear was that life would get smaller. What actually happened is that life got real — with all the weight and texture and unpredictability that word implies.

Rumi's line lands here because it's honest about the cost. The opening in me came through the breaking. I don't romanticize that, and I don't recommend the long way around. But the light does get in through the places we couldn't patch ourselves. A summer Saturday, sober, is one of the quiet proofs. Nothing dramatic has to happen today. Showing up for it is the whole thing.
reflection.meditation: Notice one ordinary moment today and let it be enough.

affirmations: I am building a life I don't need to escape from.
Today I get to be present for what actually happens, not just what I remember through a fog.
I am capable of a full Saturday — plans, people, quiet, all of it — without a drink in my hand.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for a summer morning I can remember. Grateful for the people who stayed while I figured this out, and the ones I've met since who never knew the earlier version of me. Grateful that a Saturday in August is no longer something to survive or fuel — it's just a day, offered fresh, mine to walk into.
gratitude.closing: One day. This one. That's the whole assignment.
